en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Seventeenth Chapter
The Discussion on Whether It Should Not Be Said That What Is Given to the Saṅgha Bears Great Fruit:
Should it not be said that “what is given to the Saṅgha bears great fruit”?
“Yes.
“But is it not true that the Saṅgha is worthy of offerings, worthy of hospitality, worthy of gifts, worthy of reverential salutation, and is an unsurpassed field of merit for the world?
“Yes.”
If the Saṅgha is worthy of offerings … [and so on] … an unsurpassed field of merit for the world, then indeed it should be said:
“What is given to the Saṅgha is of great fruit.
It should not be said that [it is not so].
“Is it not the case that what is given to the Saṅgha bears great fruit?”—
“Yes.”—
“But has the Blessed One not declared that there are four pairs of persons, eight individual persons, who are worthy of offerings?”
“Yes.
“If it is true that four pairs of persons, eight types of individuals, have been declared by the Blessed One to be worthy of offerings, then indeed, sir, it must be said:
‘What is given to the Saṅgha is of great fruit.’”
Is it not to be said that "what is given to the Saṅgha is of great fruit"?
Yes, it is.
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“Give to the Saṅgha, Gotamī; when you have given to the Saṅgha, both I and the Saṅgha will be honored”?
Does such a sutta exist?
“Yes.
[If so,] then it must follow that what is given to the Saṅgha is of great fruit.
It should not be said [that it is not].
“Is it not the case that what is given to the Saṅgha bears great fruit?
— “Yes.
— “Did not Sakka, lord of the devas, say this to the Blessed One:”
“For human beings who are making offerings,
for living beings seeking merit,
performing meritorious deeds that lead to the acquisitions of the world— ”
“Where is a gift given of great fruit?
“To the four who are practicing and the four who are established in the fruits;”
This Saṅgha is upright,
established in wisdom and virtue;
for those people who offer sacrifices, it is the most worthy recipient.
For living beings seeking merit who perform worldly meritorious deeds,
what is given to the Saṅgha yields great fruit.
For this Saṅgha is vast and sublime;
it is immeasurable like the ocean.
For these disciples, heroes among men, are indeed the best.
The light-makers proclaim the Dhamma.
Well-given, well-offered, and well-sacrificed is the gift given by those who give it specifically for the sake of the Saṅgha.
That offering, established within the Saṅgha,
yields great fruit and is praised by those who know the world.
Recalling such a sacrifice, they—
Those born of the Vedas who wander in the world,
having eradicated the stain of stinginess along with its root,
blameless, they go to the heavenly realm.
Is that indeed the Sutta? Yes.
Therefore, what is given to the Saṅgha is of great fruit.
It should not be said that what is given to the Saṅgha yields little fruit. The discussion on this is concluded.
